sagitta, sagittae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

The ordinary word in prose and verse (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • cum arcum mihi et pharetram et sagittās sūmpserō

    when I’ve taken up my bow and quiver and arrowsPlaut. Trin. 3.2.99 (Lewis & Short)

See also bow.
